description: Higher-level image understanding: keypoints and feature matching, registration and alignment, optical flow, face and object detection, OCR, barcodes, and neural-network-backed content recognition and restyling.

tools.name: ImageKeypoints
tools.description: Finds distinctive keypoints in an image and optionally returns their descriptors, scales and orientations. Methods include SURF, ORB, BRISK and KAZE variants. Keypoints are the basis for matching, stitching and object recognition.

tools.name: ImageCorrespondingPoints
tools.description: Finds matching keypoints between two images and returns two lists of corresponding coordinates. These correspondences drive registration, panorama stitching and stereo geometry. Matching method and transformation class can be constrained.
tools.notes: Pass the result to FindGeometricTransform to estimate the mapping between the images.

tools.name: FindGeometricTransform
tools.description: Estimates the geometric transformation that best maps one set of points, or one image, onto another. It supports translation, rigid, similarity, affine and perspective classes, with robust RANSAC-style fitting. Use it for registration, rectification and panorama alignment.

tools.name: ImageAlign
tools.description: Aligns one image to a reference image by estimating and applying a geometric transformation. It hides the keypoint matching and fitting steps behind one call. Use it before differencing, averaging or stacking images of the same scene.

tools.name: ImageFeatureTrack
tools.description: Tracks image features across a sequence of frames, returning their positions in each frame. Missing entries indicate features that were lost. Use it for motion analysis, video stabilization and particle tracking.
tools.notes: ImageDisplacements computes a dense optical-flow field instead of sparse tracks.

tools.name: ImageDisplacements
tools.description: Computes a dense optical-flow field giving the estimated displacement of every pixel between successive frames. The result is an array of vectors that can be visualized with ListStreamPlot or ListVectorPlot. Use it for motion segmentation and velocimetry.

tools.name: FindFaces
tools.description: Detects human faces in an image and returns their bounding rectangles, or the cropped face images. A minimum size can be given to skip small detections. Use it as a preprocessing step for recognition, blurring or cropping.
tools.notes: For general object detection use ImageContents or a detector network from NetModel.

tools.name: ImageIdentify
tools.description: Identifies what an image depicts, returning an Entity or a list of ranked candidates with probabilities. It uses a built-in neural network trained on thousands of everyday categories. Use it for quick classification when you do not want to train your own model.
tools.notes: Requires the identification network, which downloads on first use.

tools.name: ImageContents
tools.description: Detects objects in an image and returns a Dataset of their bounding boxes, classes, confidences and cropped images. It performs full object detection rather than whole-image classification. Use it to inventory the contents of photographs.

tools.name: ImageCases
tools.description: Finds all instances of specified object categories in an image and returns the matching sub-images or their positions. It is the pattern-matching style interface to object detection. Use it to extract every occurrence of a class from a picture.

tools.name: TextRecognize
tools.description: Performs optical character recognition on an image, returning the recognized text. Structural levels such as "Word" or "Line" return bounding boxes and confidences instead of plain text. Language can be specified to improve accuracy.
tools.notes: Binarize and deskew the image first for noisy scans; FindImageText gives text regions without recognition.

tools.name: FindImageText
tools.description: Locates regions of an image that contain text, returning their bounding boxes at character, word, line or block level. It separates detection from recognition, which is useful for layout analysis. Combine it with TextRecognize on each region.
tools.example:
img = Rasterize[Column[{"line one", "line two"}], ImageResolution -> 150];
FindImageText[img, "Line"]

tools.name: BarcodeRecognize
tools.description: Reads barcodes and QR codes from an image, returning the encoded string and optionally the format and position. Many 1D and 2D symbologies are supported. Use it for inventory, ticketing and document workflows.

tools.name: BarcodeImage
tools.description: Generates a barcode or QR code image from a string in a chosen symbology. Size and error-correction level can be specified. Use it to produce labels, tickets and machine-readable links.

tools.name: ImageRestyle
tools.description: Re-renders an image in the visual style of another image or a named style, using a neural style-transfer network. The strength of the effect can be tuned. Use it for artistic rendering and visual experimentation.
tools.usage:
ImageRestyle[image, style]
ImageRestyle[image, {w1 -> style1, w2 -> style2}]
tools.notes: Downloads a neural network on first use and is computationally expensive.

tools.name: ImageSaliencyFilter
tools.description: Produces a saliency map highlighting the regions of an image that stand out perceptually. It is useful for automatic cropping, attention modelling and region-of-interest selection. The output is a grayscale image of saliency scores.

tools.name: ImageGraphics
tools.description: Converts a raster image into vector graphics primitives by tracing regions of similar color. The number of colors and the detail level are controllable. Use it to vectorize logos, maps and line drawings for scalable output.

tools.name: HighlightImage
tools.description: Draws highlights such as points, rectangles, masks or regions on top of an image, with automatic styling. It is the standard way to display detection or segmentation results. Multiple highlight groups can be styled differently.

tools.name: ImagePyramid
tools.description: Builds a multi-resolution pyramid of an image, either Gaussian or Laplacian. Pyramids underpin scale-space analysis, blending and efficient multi-scale search. InverseImagePyramid reconstructs the original from a Laplacian pyramid.

tools.name: ImageInstanceQ
tools.description: Tests whether an image contains an instance of a given concept or entity, returning True or False. It provides a simple semantic filter over image collections. A threshold controls how confident the answer must be.
tools.usage:
ImageInstanceQ[image, category]
ImageInstanceQ[image, category, AcceptanceThreshold -> t]

tools.name: ImageQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid Image object, returning True or False. It is the standard type guard in image-processing code and pattern definitions. Use it in patterns such as img_?ImageQ to make definitions apply only to images.
